question: What visual feature distinguishes the 'separate intersections' case from the 'single intersection' case in Figure 2A-5?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The distinguishing visual feature is whether the paths of opposing left-turning vehicles cross each other in the median area. In the "A – Separate intersections" panel, the median is wide and the two blue left-turn paths cross each other within the median opening; in the "B – Single intersection" panel, the median is narrow and the opposing left-turn paths curve inside one another without crossing. Standards (mandatory): - "On unsignalized minor-street approaches from which both left turns and right turns are permitted onto a divided highway at a crossing that functions as two separate intersections (see Section 2A.23), except as provided in Paragraph 2 of this Section, a Divided Highway Crossing (R6-3 or R6-3a) sign (see Figure 2B-13) shall be used to advise road users that they are approaching an intersection with a divided highway (see Figure 2B-19)." - "At the crossing of a roadway with a divided highway that functions as two separate intersections, ONE WAY signs shall be placed, visible to each crossroad approach, on the near right and far left corners of each intersection with the directional roadways (see Figure 2B-19)." Guidance (recommended): - A divided highway crossing should be signed and marked as separate intersections when both of the following conditions are present: (A) the paths of opposing left turns from the divided highway cross each other (see Figure 2A-5), and (B) there is adequate storage in the interior approaches for the design vehicles expected to cross the divided highway. - At the crossing of two divided highways, engineering judgment should be used to determine the number of separate intersections. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-5 shows panel A labeled "Separate intersections (paths of opposing left-turning vehicles cross)," where the blue left-turn path arrows visibly intersect within a wide median, versus panel B labeled "Single intersection (paths of opposing left-turning vehicles do not cross)," where the narrow median forces the left-turn paths to curve around each other without crossing. - [Image 2] Page 105 (full page view of Figure 2A-5) confirms the same contrast: the wide-median layout in panel A produces crossing left-turn paths, while the narrow-median layout in panel B produces non-crossing paths. - [Image 3] Page 93 shows Figure 2A-3 (sign placement at intersections) and does not bear on this distinction. - [Image 4] Page 1145 shows Figure 9E-10 (two-stage bicycle turn boxes) and does not bear on this distinction. - [Image 5] Page 588 shows Figure 3B-7 (two-way left-turn lane markings) and does not bear on this distinction. Citations: - Section 2A.23 Guidance §1 (p.63) - Section 2A.23 Guidance §3 (p.64) - Section 2B.50 Standard §1 (p.116) - Section 2B.49 Standard §3 (p.114) - Figure 2A-5 (p.64) - Page 105
gold_answer: In the separate-intersections case, the paths of opposing left-turning vehicles cross; in the single-intersection case, those paths do not cross.
